newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Acordia's buyers see IPO in 3-5 years.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Acordia's buyers see IPO in 3-5 years.

text.p: One of the parties involved in buying U.S. insurance broker Acordia Inc said he expected to sell a small stake in the company back to the public three to five years after taking it private.

Such a strategy would give institutional investors and management an opportunity to cash out of their investment if they so choose and provide the company with common stock to use as currency for acquisitions, said Bruce Schnitzer, chairman of Wand Partners Inc, one of the proposed buyers of Acordia.
However, Schnitzer, speaking to Reuters in a telephone interview on Thursday, said the buyers did not plan to "flip" their investment, by seeking a quick sale to turn a profit.
"The institutional investors will want some kind of liquidity within, say, five years," Schnitzer said.

Wand Partners, a New York-based private equity investment firm, and Knightsbridge Capital LLC, agreed last week to cosponsor a management group buyout of Indianapolis-based Acordia from its majority shareholder Anthem Inc.

"There's a reasonable chunk of the company that will be owned by the management; this is obviously a chance for them to become wealthy, so they're going to want some kind of liquidity," he said. "And if you're really going to be a consolidator, you'd really be better off with a public stock."

"So, for a lot of reasons, it is likely that in three to five years you would bring Acordia to the public through an IPO (initial public offering) and create a public company that would continue to be owner managed," he said.
But, he stressed, "It's not a quick flip.

The agreement calls for the equity group to pay $320 million, including the assumption of about $40 million of debt and a $10 million contingent payment based upon future operating earnings. The transaction is expected to close at the end of August.
Under the terms, the management group will hold a "significant minority" stake in Acordia, with the remainder about evenly split between Wand Partners and Knightsbridge Capital, Schnitzer said.

Investors in Wand Partners include the University of Texas Investment Management Co, Banc One Corp's Banc One Capital, and a group of insurance companies, including New York-based insurance holding company PennCorp Financial Group Inc, and Allstate Corp, Schnitzer said.
Knightsbridge Capital LLC is the general partner of Knightsbridge Capital I LP, an investment fund affiliated PennCorp.
Other investors include High Ridge Capital Partners LP, a private equity fund that invests exclusively in the property-casualty industry.
Major investors in High Ridge, which invested Acordia in conjunction with Wand Partners, include Chartwell Re Corp, Schnitzer said.
NationsBank Capital Investors, which worked with Knightsbridge Capital, also was among the equity investors.
Acordia, the world's seventh-largest insurance broker, has made 61 acquisitions since 1991.

Schnitzer said he expected the company to grow further through the acquisition of other regional, middle-market brokers as it carves out a niche outside areas dominated by Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc and Aon Corp, the world's two heavyweight brokers.
In addition, he said, Acordia needs to strengthen its international business.
"There is a need for an international network," he said.
"It's not the dominant focus, but it's important and so you probably will see adding either by acquisition or by some other form of affiliation a more robust international network," Schnitzer said.
In addition, he expects to see further consolidation among the world's second tier of insurance brokers.
"Probably not so much Marsh and Aon, who really are dominant, but amongst the next tier," he said.
"And, so we'll certainly be on the lookout for any combination that works for both sides in (any) sort of larger combinations," he said.
